findings.issue: sortRows encodes the spec's trickiest rules — missing values last in both directions (line 216), ascending/descending flip, move-name tie-break (line 224) — with no tests; the both-missing tie-break (line 213) is already direction-inconsistent
findings.suggestion: Extract sortRows to lib and add a table-driven unit test over a fixture row set covering each column, both directions, and missing values

findings.issue: Dedup key `${method}:${move name}` silently drops rows where a Pokémon learns the same move at multiple levels in one version group, a real pattern in PokéAPI data; no test would catch this or a future change to it
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getPokemonMoveInfo against a synthetic pokemon.moves fixture with duplicate level-up entries, plus ordering by version-group order and default-game selection

findings.issue: Home route combines three filters, search substring matching, page clamping and slice math with no tests; regressions show as inconsistent UI ('No Pokémon found' with count '1025 Pokémon') rather than errors
findings.suggestion: Test the pure pieces separately: normalizePage, buildQuery (omitting defaults, encoding q with spaces), and a filter/slice helper over a small fake catalog

findings.issue: htmx fragment endpoint /pokemon/:name/moves-table has untested parameter validation (sort whitelist, dir, unknown method → 404) and is only reachable via the acceptance suite's click paths
findings.suggestion: Integration-test the route directly (app.request()) asserting 404 on bad method/sort and a rendered table with aria-sort on valid input

findings.issue: Promise cache correctness (evicting failed entries so a transient API error isn't sticky for the process) is untested; this is the exact mechanism the live-data-overlay scenario relies on
findings.suggestion: Unit-test cached() with a loader that rejects once then succeeds, asserting the second call retries

findings.issue: Pure spec-mandated formatters (humanize, dexNumber padStart(4), statLabel mappings, latestEnglishFlavorText whitespace collapse, height/weight decimals) have zero unit tests despite being the most refactor-vulnerable code
findings.suggestion: Add a plain-node test file (node:test, no dependencies needed) covering humanize('mr-mime'), '#0025', Sp. Atk/Sp. Def labels, and \f collapsing

findings.issue: htmx-vs-full-page branching (isHtmx) decides fragment vs document for both '/' and '/pokemon/:name', including HX-Push-Url header correctness — nothing covers the fragment contract
findings.suggestion: Integration tests asserting HX-Request:true returns only the fragment plus a correct HX-Push-Url, and that page 1 URLs drop the page param

findings.issue: Error handling is untested: only NotFoundError is caught per route; any other API failure yields a plain-text 500 with no layout, and the '/' route has no error handling at all
findings.suggestion: A couple of integration tests with a stubbed API returning 500/404 to pin the 404 page and onError contract

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion boundary (id !== null && id <= 10000) appears in three places (speciesRefsToCards:84, abilities:668, types:739); a refactor that changes one copy but not the others would show Mega forms on some pages only
findings.suggestion: Extract one isSpeciesId(id) helper and test it at the boundary values (10000, 10001)

findings.issue: No test script or runner at all; adding tests later requires bootstrapping from zero, which raises the cost of the very refactor protection tests would provide
findings.suggestion: Add a 'test' script using node:test (already in Node 24, zero deps) and start with the pure-function tests above

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no test script, runner, or test files — despite being largely built from pure functions (formatters, a sort comparator, a moves-dedup pipeline, pagination and URL-state helpers) that would be trivial to unit-test. Every guard currently comes from the harness-owned Playwright suite, so a refactor of the data layer or sorting logic could break spec-mandated behaviour with nothing in the repo failing. The riskiest untested code is sortRows' missing-values-last-in-both-directions rule, the per-method move dedup that can silently drop legitimate rows, and the home route's filter/pagination/slice math.

untested.likelyBug: A direction-aware comparator refactor makes missing power/accuracy sort first when descending, or the both-missing tie-break flips, silently breaking the spec's ordering with no failing test
